title: Northern lights
summary: Catch an aurora when the forecast spikes.

media.alt: Green aurora arching over a snowy field at night

blocks.note: Bright, fast-moving curtains: short end (1–4 s). Faint glow: long end.

blocks.text: In central Europe an aurora needs a **strong storm (Kp 7 or more)**. Watch an aurora app or the NOAA Kp forecast, then look **north, low on the horizon**. The camera often sees colour your eyes can't.

steps: Check the Kp forecast and cloud cover. Go somewhere dark with a clear view north.
Tripod down. Frame some foreground: trees, a hut, water to reflect the colour.
Manual focus: magnify the live view on a bright star until it's the smallest point. Tape the ring.
Widest aperture, ISO 3200, 8 s. White balance about 3500 K.
Use the 2 s timer. Shoot, then check: streaky curtains mean shorten the shutter; too dark means raise ISO.
Keep shooting. Displays come in waves, often around midnight, and can fade and return.

items: Cold drains batteries fast. Keep the spare in an inside pocket.
Shoot RAW: the colour of an aurora is hard to get right in a JPEG.
Lens fogging up? A hand warmer held to the lens with a rubber band stops dew.

after.text: Same setup as the Milky Way guide

steps: **Mode dial to M**. Aperture wide open, **ISO 3200**.
Switch to **MF**. Magnify the live view on a bright star and turn the ring until it's a point.
Shutter **8 s** to start: 1–4 s for fast curtains, up to 15 s for a faint glow.
**MENU › Shooting 3 › White balance › K** and set about **3500 K**.
**MENU › Shooting 7 › Drive mode › Self-timer: 2 sec** (or the BR-E1 remote).
Lens IS off on the tripod: the R10 has no in-body stabiliser, so the lens switch is the one that matters.
Shoot RAW (**Shooting 1 › Image quality**) and check the result. Adjust shutter first, then ISO.
canon-r10.note: Already saved your Milky Way setup to C1? Turn the dial to C1 and only change the shutter and white balance.
